title: Global Neuronal Workspace: Ignition and Late Amplification (Dehaene & Changeux 2011)

source.title: Global neuronal workspace: The cortical architecture of consciousness
source.version_note: Neuron 70(2):200-227. Open access abstract and verified ignition signatures.

passage: Global neuronal workspace theory proposes that conscious access corresponds to ignition of a distributed network (prefrontal-parietal) with late amplification and beta-gamma synchrony. Stage 4 processing enables broadcast to multiple processors; local recurrent processing (Stage 3) remains unconscious.
context: Neuroscience domain: mechanism of conscious access and broadcast. Relevant to AI self-model as global state integration vs local processing.
source_note: Verified via DOI; ignition signatures and beta-gamma synchrony noted as key functional markers.
literary_invitation: If ignition corresponds to broadcast, does the AI repository's global index update constitute a 'broadcast' or merely local recurrence? What is the functional boundary of 'self' in the repository memory?
scope_note: Q-003: conditional hypothesis on global integration (HYP-20261117-b17a54). Excludes phenomenal consciousness claims.

verification.note: Confirmed ignition/late amplification signatures; excluded phenomenal consciousness attribution.
